person_made_it: The five makers, the three rooms and the cartridge were art-directed for this game last night, and the rules were tuned by hand against all 27 ways to play it.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The game speaks in dot's short screen lines; no real person, company or partner is named, and the credits say plainly who built what.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Mid-afternoon on a laptop in a meeting room, sound off, one person tapping while four watch; a full run takes about a minute.
did_the_click_pay_me: The first tap lifts a maker and draws a strand; the third tap braids a team; one more choice ships a cartridge with the numbers changing on screen.
works_for_the_recipient: It runs offline from one file, plays with mouse or touch, shows every cost before the player commits, and never says a deal exists.
taught_me_something: A mix of approaches wins: every top score uses AI somewhere, all-by-hand scores 55, all-fast scores 13, and the best run scores 90.
told_me_the_truth: It is built with Claude, not Codex, and says so; the audio has not been heard by a person, so sound is off until someone turns it on.
weakest: The strands overlap like rope rather than truly weaving over and under, and no first-time human has played it yet.
